alt: Two sorted lists, A and B, each with its own index pointer, i and j. At each step the smaller of the two pointed-at values moves into the merged result and that pointer advances. When one list runs out, the rest of the other list is copied over unchanged, since it is already sorted.

steps.caption: i starts at index 0 of A, j starts at index 0 of B. merged is empty.
A[0] = 1 is at most B[0] = 2, so it comes next. merged so far: [1]. i advances.
B[0] = 2 is smaller than A[1] = 3, so it comes next. merged so far: [1, 2]. j advances.
A[1] = 3 is at most B[1] = 4, so it comes next. merged so far: [1, 2, 3]. i advances.
B[1] = 4 is smaller than A[2] = 5, so it comes next. merged so far: [1, 2, 3, 4]. j advances.
A[2] = 5 is at most B[2] = 6, so it comes next. merged so far: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. i advances.
B[2] = 6 is smaller than A[3] = 7, so it comes next. merged so far: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]. j advances.
A[3] = 7 is at most B[3] = 8, so it comes next. merged so far: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]. i advances.
A is exhausted. The rest of B, [8], is already sorted, so it is copied over as is. merged: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8].
i starts at index 0 of A, j starts at index 0 of B. merged is empty.
A[0] = 1 is at most B[0] = 3, so it comes next. merged so far: [1]. i advances.
A[1] = 2 is at most B[0] = 3, so it comes next. merged so far: [1, 2]. i advances.
A is exhausted. The rest of B, [3, 4, 5, 6, 7], is already sorted, so it is copied over as is. merged: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7].
i starts at index 0 of A, j starts at index 0 of B. merged is empty.
A[0] = 2 is at most B[0] = 2, so it comes next. merged so far: [2]. i advances.
A[1] = 2 is at most B[0] = 2, so it comes next. merged so far: [2, 2]. i advances.
B[0] = 2 is smaller than A[2] = 4, so it comes next. merged so far: [2, 2, 2]. j advances.
B[1] = 3 is smaller than A[2] = 4, so it comes next. merged so far: [2, 2, 2, 3]. j advances.
B is exhausted. The rest of A, [4], is already sorted, so it is copied over as is. merged: [2, 2, 2, 3, 4].
